speaker: Doctor

DIAGNOSIS READY: Ovarian Carcinoma with Malignant Ascites.

The patient is a 40-year-old nulliparous woman presenting with shortness of breath and rapid abdominal girth increase due to a large ovarian mass. These findings suggest an advanced malignancy causing significant ascites and potential pleural effusion. Based on the clinical picture of a large ovarian mass and systemic symptoms, I recommend requesting a CT Abdomen and Pelvis with contrast to assess tumor extent and fluid volume, as well as a Thoracentesis if respiratory distress persists.
